pageCache.pageTitle: Chelsfield Primary School - Mission, Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Vision and Values
At Chelsfield we strive to develop happy, motivated and successful learners who are ambitious and well equipped to meet all future challenges.
Our core values are held at the heart of everything we do:
Confidence and self-belief.
Kindness and compassion.
Independence and resilience.
We have a “can do” attitude.
SOLA Mission, Vision and Values
SOLA is a family of schools committed to the pursuit of excellence for our pupils. We recognise our responsibility to play a central role within our community, and to continually improve, together.
Is for every child in a SOLA school to be included, to know that they are important and to acquire and develop the tools, character and values that will enable them to be happy, to contribute, and to thrive throughout their lives.
Characteristics and Values:
The characteristics and values that mean most to us and that we will promote are kindness, curiosity, honesty, respect, inclusivity, responsibility and resilience.

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Chelsfield Primary School
Dear Families and Visitors,
As the Headteacher of Chelsfield Primary School and Pratts Bottom Primary School, I am delighted to welcome you to our vibrant learning community. Our schools are dedicated to providing a nurturing environment where every child can thrive, develop, and succeed.
Personalised Attention
At our small schools, we pride ourselves on offering personalised attention to each child. Our dedicated staff members know every child well, fostering strong relationships that create a profound sense of belonging. This close-knit community spirit ensures that both staff and children support one another, creating a family-like atmosphere where everyone feels valued.
Focus on Wellbeing
We believe that the wellbeing of our children is paramount. Our holistic approach prioritises emotional and mental health alongside academic success. Through tailored programmes, we teach self-regulation and emotional understanding, equipping children with essential life skills. Our proactive conflict resolution strategies help maintain a peaceful learning environment, teaching children valuable interpersonal skills that will serve them well throughout their lives.
Ambition for Learning
Our commitment to high aspirations drives us to challenge and motivate our children to reach their full potential. We design our curriculum to equip them with the knowledge and skills necessary for their next educational steps, ensuring they are well-prepared for future challenges. We instil a love for learning that inspires children to explore, inquire, and grow.
Positive Impact on Society
At Chelsfield Primary School, we are dedicated to values-driven education. By instilling principles such as kindness, unity, and ambition, we shape our children to become responsible and impactful members of society. We provide numerous opportunities for community engagement, fostering a sense of responsibility and encouraging our children to contribute positively to the world around them.
Quality of Teaching
Our team of dedicated staff is committed to delivering high-quality teaching tailored to meet the diverse needs of all children. We embrace a culture of continuous improvement, ensuring that our instructional practises are effective and innovative. This commitment to professional development supports ongoing enhancements in teaching methods and educational outcomes.
In conclusion, I invite you to explore our website and learn more about the wonderful opportunities available at Chelsfield Primary School and Pratts Bottom Primary School. Together, we can nurture the next generation of learners, leaders, and compassionate citizens.

Stars Breakfast Club
Breakfast Club : 7.45am-8.50am
The Chelsfield Primary School Stars Breakfast Club is open to all our school children from Reception to Year 6. The club is run by school staff on site here at Chelsfield.
We aim to provide high quality care which meets the needs of both parents and children. For parents, this means knowing that your child is safe and happy in a club that is reliable and offers a consistent service.
For a child this means an environment that is safe, supportive and encouraging. It is a place to be with friends and make new ones.
Stars Breakfast is open from 7.45am until 8.50am - the children have the opportunity to have breakfast if they would like. A sample menu can be seen below.
The Club will not operate during school holidays and inset days when the school is closed to pupils.
All sessions must be paid for at the time of booking via our online booking and payment system Arbor, or by childcare vouchers in advance. When booking you can choose the sessions you would like your child to attend.
Places will be allocated on a first come basis. We are able to be flexible with regular and ADHOC attendance at the present time.

Modern Foreign Languages
French
Intent
At Chelsfield it is our hope that all our pupils will develop a genuine interest and curiosity about languages, finding them enjoyable and exciting, and show a desire to continue their language learning past Key Stage Two. Learning a second language offers pupils the opportunity to explore relationships between language and identity, develop a deeper understanding of other cultures and the world around them with a better awareness of self, others and cultural differences.
Here at Chelsfield, we have chosen to teach French. The French curriculum at our school develops knowledge beyond the everyday experience of the children, and inspires pupils to want to know more about the world in which they live. It provides them with the skills needed to be able to engage with the wider world.
Implementation
Children develop their love of language, learning and develop skills throughout their time in KS2 at Chelsfield. Our scheme of work, Language Angels, focuses on speaking, listening, reading and writing skills, as well as making children aware of grammatical features of the French language. We follow the sequence of lessons from this scheme of work adapted to suit our pupils covering a wide variety of topics and themes. Previous language will be revised, recalled and consolidated whenever possible and appropriate. Performing is a key part of pupils’ French learning. The opportunities that we plan for this includes singing songs, drama and role play activities, and performing rhymes and poems. To provide children with an audience and purpose, and to make learning more memorable, we have various opportunities throughout the year to perform to parents and carers. Using 5 minute French lessons and using French in the everyday classroom for the register, birthday's, counting, and classroom instructions throughout the week to supplement and practise learning will also be encouraged. KS1 will be introduced to MFL through these methods.

Meet the Governors
Meet the Governors (ID 1027)
Brian Ford Vulnerable Groups
Brian Ford
I have lived in the Borough of Bromley since 2008 and am relishing the opportunity to serve as a Governor, as I have two children attending Pratts Bottom Primary School. Being involved in supporting the school from a strategic perspective is something I am looking forward to. I am grateful to be able to help the school that provides our children and community with key core values.
Louise Baxendale Personal Development & Wellbeing
Louise Baxendale
I am Louise Baxendale, a mother of a child starting year 1 at Pratts Bottom Primary School. My family moved to Pratts Bottom in January 2021 and we were keen for our daughter to begin her education at the small local school. I have loved joining the community of both the village and of the school and have enjoyed getting to know the education framework and feeling like we're part of the schools' 'family'.
I am a civil engineer and have worked in the engineering industry for 13 years. I am currently working as an Associate for an engineering consultancy, mainly working on trying to improve the strategic road network (motorways). At my previous role working for National Highways (government owned company), I led a national team developing technical standards, strategies and programmes to improve the day to day operations of motorways.
I am a STEM ambassador (volunteering programme to promote and support STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics) in schools and colleges) and I am keen to influence this within Pratts Bottom. I love that Pratts Bottom Primary School's mission is that 'every child can succeed because they are recognised and valued.' This is so important along with nourishing the children with support in their education, a crucial stepping stone into their future education and working lives. I am passionate about the shaping and supporting of the children's education and wider environment to enable them to reach their full potential and I hope to be part of a team that can make a difference.
Dann Cleveland Health & Safety
Dann Cleveland
I have worked for 20 years as a Finance professional in the City and live locally. For the past four years I've been working for the National Citizens Service whose mission is to inspire generations of citizens through shared experiences that develop character and bridge social divides. I am passionate about enrichment activities and social action and also keen to bring my experience of finance, governance, risk and commercial to support the school where I can.
Chitranga Diyasena Equality, Diversity & Inclusion
Chitranga Diyasena
I have been working in various parts of the world for more than thirty years. During my stay in Malawi, Central Africa, I served as a parent governor in the governing board of Hillview Primary School, an international primary school, where my daughter started her education. I enjoyed that role and worked with management to improve schooling experiences for young children.
It is my belief that I can share my knowledge and experience with Pratts Bottom Primary School to enhance its strategic goals.
Sophie Perez EYFS
Sophie Perez
I have worked at Pratts Bottom for seven years now and have thoroughly enjoyed my time so far. There is such a wonderful community here and the children are so supportive of one other. When the opportunity arose to be become a staff governor, I jumped at the chance. I look forward to helping the school grow even further and continuing to provide all the opportunities we can for the children.
Peter Thompson Safeguarding
Peter Thompson
I believe in the school's core values, having the community at its heart. I am a Detective Inspector with 20 years service specialising in Safeguarding, protecting vulnerable adults and children. As a senior leader I have responsibility for strategic decisions delivering successful outcomes. I want the school to be a safe and nurturing place where our children can fulfil their full potential. I am keen to support the school to improve but equally hold the leadership to account when necessary.
Dr Luke Beattie
I began my career as an actor and theatre director in Canada and earned certification in Teaching English as a Second Language (2002), before attending the University of Exeter for an MFA in Staging Shakespeare, graduating with Distinction (2008), along with certifications in radio presenting and stage combat. I moved straight into a full scholarship Drama PhD with Exeter, with my thesis based on Early Modern English dramaturgy (2012). My ongoing areas of research include English dramaturgy before Shakespeare, and the history of rhetoric. Since my PhD, I have continued working as an actor, with professional credits in all media. I have also worked extensively as an educator, with students from the earliest years through to postgraduate students, as a private tutor, guest secondary school instructor, visiting director and tutor at various universities and drama schools, and for several years as the department head responsible for all academic work and contextual studies at the Italia Conti drama school for their BA in professional actor training. My children currently attend Chelsfield Primary School, and I believe my experience will be valuable to the Local Governing Board.

My wish to serve as a school governor comes from my experiences of volunteering at a local primary for the last three years. The quality of the teaching and the warmth and care with which all pupils are treated has been inspiring - and I am keen to help further.
My own background is in journalism and business publishing. I live in Chelsfield and both my - now very grown up - children were educated locally.

Music
Intention
At Chelsfield Primary School, our music curriculum intends to inspire creativity, self-expression and to encourage our children on their musical journeys, as well as giving them opportunities to connect with others. We hope to foster a lifelong love of music by exposing them to diverse musical experiences and igniting a passion for music. By listening and responding to different musical styles, finding their voices as singers, performers and as composers, all will enable them to become confident, reflective musicians.
Implementation
The music curriculum ensures children sing, listen, play, perform and evaluate. This is embedded in the classroom activities as well as the weekly singing assemblies, various concerts and performances, and the learning of instruments. Through the musical program Charanga, teachers are able to produce inclusive lessons for all children to access the musical curriculum in a fun and engaging way, further promoting a love of learning. Teachers deliver music following the Charanga programme, designed specifically for the teaching of music in primary schools. Charanga lessons are planned in sequences to provide children with the opportunities to review, remember, deepen and apply their understanding. The elements of music are taught in classroom lessons so that children are able to use some of the language of music to dissect it, and understand how it is made, played, appreciated and analysed. In the classroom children learn how to play the recorder and the glockenspiel. Playing various instruments enables children to use a range of methods to create notes, as well as how to read basic music notation. They also learn how to compose, focusing on different dimensions of music, which in turn feeds their understanding when listening, playing, or analysing music. Composing or performing using body percussion and vocal sounds is also part of the curriculum, which develops the understanding of musical elements without the added complexity of an instrument.
Wherever possible, pupils at Chelsfield are encouraged to perform. In our weekly singing assembly, children learn a variety of songs, both traditional and popular. Bi-weekly, we have an ‘open-mic’ singing assembly. Here pupils can showcase their talents and develop their self-confidence. Singing assemblies are a chance to unite the whole school community through singing. With a half an hour of corporate music-making, the benefits are numerous. Children develop a sense of belonging to a wider community. There are boosts to pupils' emotional wellbeing, staff wellbeing and morale as well.
Impact
Music enables children to develop an understanding of culture and history, both in relation to children individually, as well as ethnicities from across the world. Children are able to enjoy music in as many ways as they choose – either as listener, creator or performer. Children have the opportunity to discuss and share their own thoughts, opinions and ideas, acknowledging and respecting that these may vary and that this is positive. They can dissect music and comprehend its parts. They can sing and feel a pulse. At Chelsfield, we aim to enable our children to use the universal language of music, within a high quality musical education, that promotes the love of music and use of talent in a variety of contexts.
At Christmas a Carol Service is held at St. Martin’s, when all children are encouraged to perform.
We have a weekly singing assembly - a mix of popular and traditional songs - at times linked to the RE and MFL curriculum. There are different clubs which meet at lunchtimes, including our popular singing club.
Performances in recent years have included the ‘Young Voices’ concert at the O2.

School Meals
We encourage all children to have a healthy and nutritional meal at lunchtime and a snack during morning break. Our meals are cooked freshly on the premises by Nourish Contract Catering.
A copy of the current menu can be found below. If you require a printed version, please come and collect one from the Office.
The Mayor of London will be funding Universal Free School Meals (UFSM) this academic year to all mainstream schools in London to help with the cost of living crisis. However it is advisable that you still apply for Pupil Premium Free School Meals if you feel you qualify. Further information can be found by scrolling down this page.

Free School Meals Explained:
Universal Infant Free School Meals Scheme (UIFSM) From September 2014 all Reception, Year 1 and Year 2 pupils attending state-funded schools will be eligible for a free school meal. This is known as Universal Infant Free School Meals (UIFSM) Scheme. The Government has decided that from this date, all pupils in Reception, year 1 and year 2 should be able to have a free school meal at lunchtime. This offer does not depend on your household income or whether you receive any benefits – every child in these classes is eligible to take up the offer. The Mayor of London has decided to extend this to all years in primary schools in London.
Free School Meals (FSM) In addition to the Universal Infant free school meals your child might be entitled to additional funding if their household income is less than £16,190. You could save up to £400 a year if your child gets free school meals and it will mean they get a healthy school cooked lunch every day. If your child is eligible for free school meals, they’ll remain eligible until they finish the phase of schooling (primary or secondary) they’re in. Registering for FREE SCHOOL MEAL entitlement is confidential.
The FSM scheme is separate to the Universal Infant Free School Meal eligibility and it is open to all years therefore it is important that you still make an application if your child is eligible.
Schools are also given additional funding by the Government for every child who is awarded Free School Meals FSM. This very important funding is used to support interventions and enrichments for all children in school to close the attainment gap.
The pupil premium means that even if you don't wish to access a free daily meal, applying will mean that this school will receive further funding.
If you think your family could qualify, please click here to apply.
Packed Lunches If your child prefers a packed lunch we encourage our children to eat a healthy packed lunch. Sweets, fizzy drinks and chocolate bars should not be included in packed lunches. For healthy packed lunch ideas please visit: https://www.nhs.uk/change4life/recipes/healthier-lunchboxes
Please ensure that the packed lunch contains no nuts or nut products (or chocolate spread which can contain nuts), due to allergies.
Any drinks should be in a plastic container or carton (no glass). Fizzy drinks should not be brought to school.
Packed lunches and water bottles should always be labelled clearly with your child's name.
School Trips For school trips we can offer your child a school prepared packed lunch. A baguette with a choice of fillings of ham, tuna or cheese, together with a piece of fruit and a biscuit.
